fatal_errors: The target coating is a multicomponent AlTiCrZrNbTa refractory high-entropy alloy, not an elemental Cr coating alloyed only with Al.
The proposed interfacial alumina barrier and Cr–Zr interdiffusion mechanism do not match the demonstrated surface Al2O3–TiO2–Cr2O3 composite oxide mechanism.
The stated 300–1000 °C exposures lasting hours to thousands of hours are largely untested; the demonstrated boundaries were 1000 °C for 60 min and 1100 °C for 30 min in flowing steam.
The hypothesis misses the non-monotonic Al dependence: approximately 10 at.% was optimal, whereas at least 17 at.% promoted Al–Ti/Al–Zr phases, oxide discontinuity, and substrate oxidation.
None of the cited evidence directly supports Al-doped Cr on zirconium alloy, alumina formation at its coating–substrate interface, or performance in reactor water and steam.
explanation: The response captures only a broad motif from the target: introducing an intermediate amount of Al can reduce oxidation mass gain and improve coating integrity in high-temperature steam. However, it reconstructs the wrong coating system, baseline, oxide location, and governing mechanism. The target used about 4 µm AlTiCrZrNbTa films and compared multiple Al contents against Al-free TiCrZrNbTa, finding a sharply non-monotonic optimum near 10 at.% Al. Protection arose from a dense external composite oxide, not an alumina layer deliberately formed at the Cr–Zr interface. The proposed experiment is comparative and potentially falsifiable for the alternative hypothesis, but it lacks multiple Al levels needed to test the optimum and uses conditions outside the demonstrated domain. Its evidence is indirect and materially unrelated, so the alternative is not adequately supported.
